translation: (Voiceover): Ohoho ohoho ohoho ohoho, ohom ohom ohom ohom ohom ohom ohom ohom

Pallavi (Chorus): You are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; hey, get up, all of you, get up, get up.. champaranga, come dance together; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother

Verse 1: The customs of the hamlet must not be abandoned.. the ways of the Koya must not be given up; the customs of the hamlet must not be abandoned.. the ways of the Koya must not be given up; shall we hunt together as a band and bring it home.. arere, shall we hunt together as a band and bring it home; shall we cook it up and eat it with relish.. champare champa.. aha ambare amba.. he he champare champa.. aha ambare amba (refrain)
You are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother

Verse 2: Do not mix with other peoples.. do not put your trust in mankind; do not mix with other peoples.. do not put your trust in mankind; once all their troubles, arere, are over.. once all their troubles are over, they slip away; they throw sand in your eyes and leave; champare champa.. aha ambare amba.. he he champare champa.. aha ambare amba
You are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother

Verse 3: We have roamed the hills and valleys.. ours is a friendship with the trees and bushes; we have roamed the hills and valleys.. ours is a friendship with the trees and bushes; Samara and Chenchu, arere, no divisions between us.. Samara and Chenchu, arere, no divisions between us; proclaim that all the hill tribes are one; champare champa.. aha ambare amba.. he he champare champa.. aha ambare amba
You are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother; you are mother to us all, O mother.. accept our salutations, O mother

Verse 4: You are the chief of the band.. you must protect the band; you are the chief of the band.. you must protect the band; like a fighting cock, arere, you must leap over the fort wall.. like a fighting cock, arere, you must leap over the fort wall; if fire comes to the hamlet, you must give your very life; champare champa.. aha ambare amba.. he he champare champa.. aha ambare amba

He jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba.. he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba; he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba.. he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba; he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba.. he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba; he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba.. he he jambara jamba.. aha ambare amba
summaryEn: Andariki Amma ('Mother to All') is sung by Balu on the album Old Is Gold Janapada Geethalu (2010). Although the archive lists it under Family, the song reads as a communal dance song of a hill-dwelling tribal community. The chorus salutes a mother figure - 'you are mother to us all, accept our salutations' - most likely a protective goddess, and calls everyone to get up and dance together. The verses are addressed to the community itself. They urge people to keep the customs of the gudem (tribal hamlet) and the ways of the Koya people, to hunt together as a band and share the meat, and to stay wary of outsiders who take help while in trouble and then 'throw sand in your eyes'. The third verse speaks of kinship with the hills, valleys and trees, and calls for unity among hill tribes, naming the Chenchu and another group sung as 'Samara'. The last verse tells the leader of the band to protect his people, leaping walls like a fighting cock and giving his life if the hamlet is attacked. Each verse ends in the rhythmic vocables 'champare champa, ambare amba', and the song closes with a long run of 'jambara jamba', suited to group dancing.
summaryTe: ‘అందరికి అమ్మ’ పాటను బాలు పాడారు. ఇది 2010 నాటి ‘ఓల్డ్ ఈజ్ గోల్డ్ జానపద గీతాలు’ ఆల్బమ్‌లోనిది. ఆర్కైవ్‌లో ‘కుటుంబం’ విభాగంలో ఉన్నా, పాటంతా కొండ ప్రాంత ఆదివాసీ సమూహం కలిసి ఆడిపాడే నృత్యగీతంలా సాగుతుంది. పల్లవిలో ‘అందరికి అమ్మవు నీవు, వందనాలు గైకొనవే’ అంటూ ఒక తల్లిని - బహుశా రక్షించే గ్రామదేవతను - నమస్కరిస్తారు; అందరూ లేచి కలిసి ఆడమని పిలుపునిస్తారు. చరణాలు సమూహానికే చెప్పే హితవుల్లా ఉంటాయి: గూడెం ఆచారాలు, కోయ అలవాట్లు వదలవద్దు; గుంపుగా వేటాడి తెచ్చి పంచుకుని తినాలి; కష్టం తీరగానే జారుకుని ‘కళ్ళల్లో ఇసుక చల్లిపోయే’ బయటివాళ్ళను నమ్మవద్దు. మూడో చరణం కొండకోనలతో, చెట్లు చేమలతో ఉన్న చెలిమిని చెప్పి, చెంచులు, ‘సమర’ వంటి తెగల మధ్య భేదాలు వద్దని, కొండజాతి అంతా ఒక్కటేనని చాటుతుంది. చివరి చరణం గుంపు నాయకుడు కోడిపుంజులా కోట దూకి, గూడానికి ఆపద వస్తే ప్రాణమైనా ఇవ్వాలని చెబుతుంది. ప్రతి చరణం చివర ‘చంపరె చంపా, అంబరె అంబా’ అనే లయబద్ధ పదాలు, ముగింపులో ‘జంబర జంబ’ అనే దీర్ఘ ఆవృత్తి సామూహిక నృత్యానికి తగినట్లుగా ఉన్నాయి.
